title: What’s With All These Outages?
gist: WIRED's Uncanny Valley podcast attributes a week of US outages (Microsoft, FAA, Chase, United, NSA, Apple) to mundane update failures, plausibly accelerated by organizations rushing patches for bugs found with Anthropic's Mythos model, not cyberattacks. It also covers Anthropic's ~$1.5 trillion IPO (ticker ANT) amid midterm anti-data-center votes, Nvidia's $115.8 billion quarter after Jensen Huang's resignation, and a new US rule to stop Chinese firms renting advanced AI chips offshore ahead of Trump's meeting with Xi.

insights.claim: In one week, Microsoft Outlook and Teams went down for about 24 hours, the FAA imposed a nationwide ground stop of more than four hours (only the second since 9/11 and the longest since), JPMorgan Chase's problem disrupted other banks as counterparties, United delayed over a hundred flights, the NSA classified network failed and an internal update knocked out iCloud and Apple Pay; all said the incidents were not cyberattacks.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: A cluster of reliability failures across critical services raises operational-risk scrutiny and potential regulatory pressure on change management.
insights.locator: Last Thursday, Microsoft had an outage in Outlook and Teams

insights.claim: Microsoft's Outlook outage traced to a fix deployed in July that propagated across the network and was only triggered by a later update, while the FAA communications failure traced to old fiber equipment maintained by L3Harris during an update pushed on a Friday afternoon.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Aging air-traffic-control infrastructure and contractor change-management practices are a liability for L3Harris and an argument for FAA modernization spending.
insights.locator: The Microsoft Outlook issue was actually

insights.claim: WIRED's hosts argue the outage cluster may be an indirect AI effect: organizations given access to Anthropic's cybersecurity-focused Mythos model are finding previously undetectable bugs and pushing patches at a huge rate, and the more complex the fixes pushed simultaneously, the more likely something breaks.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: AI-driven bug discovery may create a near-term wave of patch-induced outages, boosting demand for safe-deployment and rollback tooling.
insights.quote: Sending patches at a huge rate, and the more complicated the bug, the more patches trying to push out at the same time, the more likely something is going to break.
insights.locator: This goes back to Anthropic's Mythos model

insights.claim: Public suspicion that the outages were attacks was amplified by distrust of the government, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio insisting there is zero evidence the incidents are related, while Trump dismissed them as 'life' for big and powerful countries.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Low institutional credibility means outage events can trigger outsized consumer panic, such as reported doomsday prepping at Costco.
insights.quote: We have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other.

insights.claim: Anthropic went public under the ticker ANT at a reported valuation of about $1.5 trillion, among the biggest IPOs ever but below the $2 trillion figure floated several months earlier.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: The valuation step-down from $2 trillion signals cooling AI sentiment after Nvidia's turmoil and midterm data-center backlash.
insights.locator: So Anthropic finally arrived on the stock market

insights.claim: Amazon will own about 15 percent and Google nearly 14 percent of newly public Anthropic, illustrating how AI financing ties the major giants together.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Anthropic's market value flows directly into Amazon and Google balance sheets, so ANT price moves are a read-through for both.
insights.locator: I mean, I think it is the bellwether, right?

insights.claim: Anthropic takes a rent-not-own approach to compute, with nearly a trillion dollars of data-center commitments flowing to other companies such as SpaceX and Google, making it a symbol of AI-industry interdependency.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Circular AI financing concentrates systemic risk: a stumble at Anthropic would hit its compute suppliers' revenue backlogs.
insights.locator: And not just that, but Anthropic, they're like a rent-not-own

insights.claim: The hosts call Anthropic the biggest pure-play AI IPO so far, contrasting it with SpaceX's recent IPO, described as a rocket company with an AI company stapled to it, and note OpenAI's listing remains a pending question.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: ANT becomes the public-market benchmark for frontier AI lab valuation until OpenAI lists.
insights.quote: SpaceX had an IPO recently, but that is a rocket company with an AI company stapled to it.
insights.locator: But it's the first, not the first, it's the biggest pure-play

insights.claim: Voters in the recent midterms overwhelmingly and bipartisanly rejected provisions supporting the data centers AI companies need, raising questions about slowdowns in AI infrastructure investment.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Local political opposition to data centers is a growing risk to AI capex timelines, power-deal pipelines and data-center REITs.

insights.claim: As a public company Anthropic will have to file 10-Ks and 10-Qs and hold earnings calls, greatly improving transparency into a notoriously closed company, though the hosts worry quarterly growth pressure may conflict with its safety mission.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Public disclosures will give investors first hard data on frontier-lab unit economics; watch for tension between growth targets and safety commitments.
insights.quote: the incentives that will make AI profitable are not necessarily the incentives that will make humanity more sustainable
insights.locator: I mean, I think one of the great things for us as journalists

insights.claim: Sam Bankman-Fried's stake in Anthropic was clawed back by the government in his bankruptcy and sold cheaply to buyers who now stand to become rich from the IPO.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Illustrates the outsized returns captured by buyers of distressed pre-IPO AI stakes.
insights.locator: Sam Bankman-Fried of all of this

insights.claim: Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, more than $6 billion ahead of expectations, in its first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned over affairs with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset and with at least one direct report.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Fundamentals remain strong despite leadership turmoil, separating operating performance from governance risk.
insights.locator: On Tuesday, the company reported its most recent earnings

insights.claim: Nvidia lost about $2 trillion in market value along with its CEO, and despite a 'Bring Back Jensen' campaign by Elon Musk, Garry Tan and other Silicon Valley leaders, the board clearly rejected Huang's return on the earnings call.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Board resolve reduces uncertainty about a Huang return; leadership succession is now the key Nvidia overhang.
insights.locator: Over the last few days, we've had a number of Silicon Valley leaders

insights.claim: Interim Nvidia CEO and former CFO Colette Kress used her first all-hands to promise employees more pay and equity to deter departures, repeatedly saying 'We got this.'
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Higher retention spending signals talent-flight risk and could pressure Nvidia's operating expenses and dilution.
insights.locator: Nvidia's first all hands after Jensen Huang left

insights.claim: Brian Barrett argues, against popular sentiment, that Nvidia will be fine long term thanks to customer lock-in, and that a smaller Nvidia facing more competition would reduce systemic risk for the economy.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Supports holding Nvidia on lock-in while expecting slower growth and an opening for competing AI chip vendors.
insights.quote: I think a smaller Nvidia with more competition is probably ... I mean, it makes less systemic risk for everybody else.
insights.locator: I don't think Jensen's coming back.

insights.claim: Before Trump's meeting with Xi Jinping, the administration advanced a rule to stop Chinese firms from accessing advanced AI chips by renting them from data centers outside China, a loophole spotlighted because Alice Huang was an executive at one such company, Megaspeed.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Closing the offshore-rental channel could cut demand at overseas GPU cloud providers serving Chinese customers and tighten Nvidia's China-adjacent revenue.
insights.locator: Right before the trip, the administration said

insights.claim: Similar chip-access rules existed under Biden and were rolled back by Trump in 2025, and officials quietly expect little AI progress on Trump's China trip because of the Nvidia spy scandal, amid a cabinet dispute between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick in which Trump has often sided with Lutnick.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Expect continued policy oscillation on China chip exports; enforcement of the new rule is uncertain.
insights.locator: Oh, I think that's a huge part of it.

insights.claim: Incoming House Oversight chair Robert Garcia issued records-preservation requests to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump over World Liberty Financial and other ventures, and to Jared Kushner over his Saudi-backed investment firm, signaling broad Democratic investigations after the midterms.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Congressional scrutiny is a headline risk for Trump-family crypto venture World Liberty Financial.
insights.locator: One last politics thing to mention

insights.claim: Leah Feiger flags unusually early and deep Black Friday sales of around 40 percent off as a possible sign that the US economy is struggling, which Sophie Kleeman calls a recession indicator.
insights.speaker: Brian Barrett
insights.so_what: Early, deep retail discounting can indicate weak consumer demand and margin pressure heading into the holiday quarter.
insights.locator: everyone is doing their Black Friday sales right now and very early
